notes.title: Signal Maze 2.0 release ! ! !
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/4d0eb27923f7ef28e78a7f24a07f5d653151a4b5.png"][/img][/p][h2]Dear Players:[/h2][p]Since the official release of “Signal Maze” version 1.0, we have received enthusiastic feedback from our players, which includes both encouragement and affirmation, as well as many valuable suggestions and constructive criticisms. Here, we would like to thank every player who has paid attention to and supported the game, and it is your attention and correction that has provided an important guideline for our optimization direction.[/p][p]After an in-depth review by our team, we realized that due to the lack of development experience, the game has failed to achieve the desired experience in some parts. The core problem was that the overall positioning of the game was blurred and fragmented - in the EA phase, we simply used “strategy puzzle” to summarize the game category, but neglected the ‘strategy’ and “puzzle” aspects of the game. However, we ignored the essential differences between “strategy” and “puzzle” games in terms of design logic, style presentation and playing experience. This lack of clarity in the positioning of the game led to a deviation between the core gameplay and the user's expectations, which in turn affected the consistency of the overall experience.[/p][p]In view of this, we decided to systematically reconstruct the underlying positioning of the game, and simultaneously launched a comprehensive remake of the shop content. After the team's unremitting efforts, the 2.0 version of Signal Maze is now officially available to everyone.[/p][p][/p][h2]Detailed update:[/h2][p]Updated Version ID: V2.2.0:[/p][list][*][p]UPDATE: Shop function completely remake.[/p][/*][*][p]UPDATE: Seed function added to the randomization process of Shop levels.[/p][/*][*][p]UPDATE: Time Panel completely remake.[/p][/*][*][p]UPDATE: Main level streamlining, all main levels remake.[/p][/*][*][p]UPDATE: Unit shapes, locks, pivots, and sliding clamp completely remake.[/p][/*][*][p]UPDATE: Level trees completely reorganized, story lines rearranged.[/p][/*][*][p]UPDATE: Heat dissipation, corruption disaster ticks remake.[/p][/*][*][p]OPTIM: Overall level difficulty adjusted and slightly reduced.[/p][/*][*][p]OPTIM: Heat Dissipation Grid and Corruption Grid remake.[/p][/*][*][p]OPTIM: New Voucher mission type added.[/p][/*][*][p]OPTIM: Increased the frequency of Push Units and Trash Units appearing in the game.[/p][/*][*][p]OPTIM: Shops now pop up automatically when arriving at a shop tick (can be turned off in options).[/p][/*][*][p]OPTIM: Mouse drag protection now adds a smarter “semi-protection” tick  (can be adjusted in options).[/p][/*][*][p]OPTIM: Optimized visual effects of cell-to-signal and cell interactions.[/p][/*][*][p]FIX: Some missing localization and formatting issues.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/9e5406b11759691ec3fa9d2dcbf5558c8bdd95d8.png"][/img][/p][h2]About Version 1.0:[/h2][p]Because version 1.0 still has some playability in the levels and store, and because some players may be more than halfway through the game, we are offering players the option to continue playing version 1.0. Simply select “Version 1.0” via the Steam Launch options at game startup to start the game normally, and then:[/p][list][*][p][b]Level Tree, Levels, Shop, and Time Panel will remain as 1.0, and some of the 2.0 updates will also be retroactively applied.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Except DEMO version, DEMO can only launch in 2.0[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Since not all levels are remaked between 1.0 and 2.0, levels with the same name completed in 1.0 will be unlocked automatically in 2.0; Vouchers unlocked in 1.0 will be carried over to 2.0 automatically, but Industry Vouchers of the same name levels can only be obtained once.[/p][p]We promise that version 1.0 will recive bug fixing update at least until the end of this year, and will remain accessible for at least 12 months.[/p][p]However, from now on, version 1.0 will no longer receive any balancing or optimezing updates.[/p][p][/p][h2]Some update details:[/h2][p]Next, we'll go into more detail about the various updates that are important for version 2.0[/p][p]Shop functionality completely remake[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/76378c56e6201999d6c7a280c6fa6f303d4515e0.png"][/img][/p][p]The Shop is a core part of the game that we felt was in dire need of a remake. Previously, the default randomization of the store was a mechanic that failed to provide enough decisions and fun for players, so we decided to completely remake the shop. The core adjustments are that the default Shop Delivery will be changed to a Selecting Delivery, while the units available for purchase within each phase will remain randomly generated.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/d512c6f0c9c20b3121acd87d998361082c1105e7.png"][/img][/p][p]And for this unit's randomization process, if the player wishes to replay based on a known state. We've also added a seeded randomization feature. It allows the player to play the store level in an expected way.[/p][p][/p][h3]Time Panel completely remake [/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/1c318fb5c978549d73606adf4c264a5e80e83a77.png"][/img][/p][p]The core functionality of the Time Panel has not been tweaked, but we have redesigned it based on the overall R.O.O.T. device visualization.[/p][p][/p][h3]Main level streamlining, all main levels remake [/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/34a1696e0c0fadef2e03079314af7a1f857627c7.png"][/img]1.0 level tree as shown,[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/1e0bc32ea8e16a29d7fb06f802a432a293591f99.png"][/img][/p][p]Below is the level tree of 2.0 (blurred to prevent spoilers). We found that the 1.0 main story was long, poorly paced, and fragmented, so we decided to significantly streamline the length of the main story in 2.0. At the same time, we've adjusted our narrative strategy: instead of forcing the main story to carry the entire plot, we've presented some of the side stories in the form of level tree branches, so that players can independently choose whether or not to deepen their experience of the side content.[/p][p][/p][h3]Unit shapes, locks, pivots, and sliding clamp completely remake. Note: [/h3][p]This part of the update will also be reflected in the 1.0 version of the game.[/p][p]1.0 Unit and clamps [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/03c57775bdf8a43fa77526523caa6390d25ae470.png"][/img]2.0 Ver：[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/8b04c901e8f3d1088af544541bd90ca9df3c1c8d.png"][/img][/p][p]We found that in version 1.0, the unit interface is not recognizable enough, and the various types of clamps(especially the pivot and sliding clamps) are only differentiated by color, which makes it difficult to identify the unit visually. Therefore, we have completely redesigned the structure of the unit and reworked the overall shape and related clamp components, hoping to optimize the visual presentation to improve the recognition efficiency and playing experience when you play.[/p][p][/p][h2]Conclusions: [/h2][p]Thanks for sticking with us till the end. It has been a hell of ride for the past six months since Signal Maze launched. Looking back, many early decisions feel painfully naive now. Being in the middle of development, there were a lot of issues that we didn't see through in time.—it took working on this 2.0 update before we finally felt, "Okay, this time we may-be fixed things right." [/p][p]The pandemic’s impact on the project was far more tangled than we ever imagined. We’ve often wondered—without those lost years, could the game have matched our vision sooner? But "what-if" don’t get us far. Our team learned as we went, and honestly? We still don’t know how to design a game at all *maybe*. [/p][p]For this version, we overhauled everything until we nearly skinned ourselves alive—fine-tuning every bit of level logic and visual feedback. At least now when we play it, we can sigh, "Worth every sleepless night." [/p][p]Truth is, making games is like nurturing a child: you know you should stay objective, but you can’t help pouring your heart into it. 2.0 isn’t some "final chapter," but it is the best answer we can offer at this stage. How far we’ll go from here? Hard to say. But as long as players keep engaging with our work, we’ll keep exploring this maze of game design. [/p][p]To everyone who critiqued or cheered us on these past months—thank you. You’ve genuinely walked a long, long road with us.[/p]

[h1]Hello everyone! [/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/f7f71142bf410b01177a50af36961dfa6136b2b4.png[/img]

notes.title: Signal Maze: Full Release on January 16, 2025!
notes.notes:
After a year and a half of Early Access on Steam and numerous updates, the puzzle game Signal Maze (formerly known as R.O.O.T) is finally launching its full 1.0 version on January 16, 2025.

In this full release, we've added a total of 150 levels, and the main levels will now feature stunning American comic-style artwork. We've also added a variety of new gameplay mechanics while fixing numerous bugs and optimizing the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/441d58a3b13d5de7e41a674594a4cf4e8665f08a.jpg[/img]

If you enjoy intricate puzzle-solving and dystopian sci-fi narratives, be sure to wishlist the game now!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2153430

Signal Maze is a dystopian-themed puzzle game that combines elements of block-pushing and pipe-connecting. You play as "Bot," a new employee in the Remote Computing Department of the Raven Titanium Corporation. Your job is to manipulate units within the R.O.O.T. system to generate profits for the company and meet your KPIs.

As you navigate your corporate life, you'll notice some unusual occurrences in the company's facilities. Driven by curiosity, Bot teams up with their hacker friend, Ace, to uncover the secrets hidden behind the corporation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/1940ad74cdb291c64402bd0539dc02ec607a914f.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/e86215b97215241960110ba92212affcd26c7e6f.png[/img]

[h3]Key Features:[/h3]

[b]Block-pushing puzzles[/b]: Move units around the grid and connect them to generate profits.

[b]Dynamic levels:[/b] Some levels have turn-based mechanics, adding a layer of strategy and challenge.

[b]150 levels[/b]: A massive amount of content to keep you entertained.

[b]Dystopian narrative[/b]: Experience a sci-fi story told through fragmented narratives and American comic-style artwork.

notes.title: NEW NAME! From now on, Signal Maze is the new name!
notes.notes:
Greeting to all operators of RavenTek,

[h1]New Name[/h1]

We have decided to officially rename our game from R.O.O.T. to Signal Maze, the game logo and the main visual would be updated as well. Please take a look:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/9e5406b11759691ec3fa9d2dcbf5558c8bdd95d8.png[/img]

Please let us know if you like it or not.

[h1]Illustration work progress update[/h1]

In the meantime, we are working on the Illustrations of the story of Signal Maze in full swing, and the last part of the game play as well. 

We are excited to share some finished arts to you guys here:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/8e344ca8423d7ee4c83dd68ca23dfce33ef3531d.png[/img]
In the above Illustration, you can see, our protagonist, Port arrives at RavenTek for his on-boarding process. As you can see, RavenTek owns multiple buildings, occupying an entire block in the center downtown area of Ravens second district. After entered Building A, which has the distinctive “RAVEN TEK” logo hangs on the wall and is intended for reception and conference, Port is guided to his department for rest of the on-boarding process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/a8545fb907d6af1efed21fd8f472c39123a5093a.png[/img]
In the above Illustration, you can see the [T.U.L.I.P] bar. Port and Esmond, who is the other protagonist of the story, often meet here, chat about their life and have a drink. This bar decoration is full of neon elements, but it doesn't feel like a cyberspace. Although, the private booths on the second floor offer private and secure internet facilities for guests to use. Guess that's the reason why Esmond is regular guest of this bar.

We hope you guys would enjoy our Illustration style, and we hope this would make you feel connected to the story of Signal Maze.

If you guys have any comments, please let us know in the Steam forum. Please continue follow us for more updates in the future!

Thank you very much!

notes.title: ROOT art update and mouse controlling completion update! ~~~ Ver 0.3 is here !!
notes.notes:
Greeting! Fellow operators!! It's been a while! Quite a while.
Of course! We haven't been goofing around this whole time.

[h3]We've got all sorts of new content for the art and mouse controlling in this update![/h3]

[h2]UI art optimization and upgrade.[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/9f646bf645ebc980d277942a332b425fd0426264.png[/img]

To be honest, we feel that the quality of the previous art is still very amateurish. We can only enhance it little by little, little by little.

In this update, the game-ending system has been overhauled.

We've changed the game-ending-abruptly mechanic, and it's much gentler now. Of course, in addition to that, we've remaked the whole visual part of the game-ending panel. Now it's “more like it”.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/8ec11e5fe13ed618b102d2c7ade2954e12d91625.png[/img]

Artistically, in addition to the game-ending panel we added unit and grid VFX and added realistic screen effects to the entire UI.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/2a1abcd3a436818de24f6ea3f6bb1562dfbf0f79.jpg[/img]

We've also made a series of fine-tuned adjustments to device lighting, details, texture, and more as well. We hope you enjoy our new art content!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/7b8130cc48ccbaf8b981ca6b22a3f763fc717f1a.jpg[/img]

[h2]Mouse controls are now available.[/h2]

Then there's the mouse controlling  part. As we stated before in the mouse branch announcement, when we first designed this project, it was on a handheld device (D.E.O.T.). There were only buttons, so the “issue” of button priority has continued, until this day!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/70cb59b258ebecaa431683bdd604833f6982601a.png[/img]

Truth be told, mouse controlling is undoubtedly a basic feature for PC games nowadays. So R.O.O.T. has been without mouse controlling is something we found is sad as well. However, the development of mouse controlling is undoubtedly a lot of work, so it has been put on hold. Until the beginning of this year, we intend to get serious about it. So there is this mouse version. Really sorry to keep you all waiting!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/5dff92127b48127c23560f0921a566ed08d55194.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/228a8a27d7639efabe9827a02623e084c599053f.png[/img]

Version Code for this update is: 0.3.05

We have done a lot of testing on mouse related content before, but R.O.O.T.'s mouse system is still very complex, so if there are any problems. We hope you can give us every feedback!

[b]We are also very much looking forward to your comments and suggestions! We hope you can enjoy our update this time![/b]

notes.title: Small-scale testing before the launch of 'Mouse Operation'
notes.notes:
To all the operators !!

As some of you may know, R.O.O.T. was originally released on a handheld device (D.E.O.T.). So we started out with only keyboard and joystick support. The lack of mouse operation was indeed a concern for us.

As more and more players talked about using simple mouse for our game. We started to develop mouse support. Finally, this "side-project" has reached the stage where it is ready to be meet you!

So we uploaded the feature to private Betas branch↓

Branch: mouse_beta
Code: mousebeta1864

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/451233bbb4bfb3d7a985661534be2312d422e818.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/d6d2eb1508fa5741f4e399f1c7601657029d36c4.png[/img]

It's a simple phrase: "mouse support", however, it's indeed a hefty project for us.

notes.title: Major Update: Signal Zone
notes.notes:
Updated Version ID: V0.2.10：

Added 30 new levels and 4 tutorial levels.
[h3]Introducing a new major core mechanism - Signal Zone[/h3]

The new levels in this update will include mechanics related to “Signal Zone,” providing players with more challenging puzzles and element arrangements.

Matrix Signal Zone: When a Matrix unit is activated, it generates a Signal Zone centered around the unit. The size of the generated field increases with the unit’s level.

Thermal Signal Zone: Similar to the Matrix Signal Zone, activated Thermal units generate Signal Zone centered around them. The size of the Signal Zone increases with the unit’s tier, and it is slightly larger than the Matrix unit’s Signal Zone. However, please note that the Signal Zone generated by Thermal units can be blocked by other units and Barricades.

Depending on the type of Signal Zone, players need to arrange signal fields until they cover specific locations and continue to yield benefits - it’s not an easy task! More types of Signal Zones will be added in future updates, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Update; V0.1.60 Task Tick Optimization
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello! Fellow operators![/h1]

It's been a while, hasn't it? We're just a little over two months away from the game's launch. Have you all been enjoying your time at 'Raventech'? XD

In this update, we're bringing you the first major one since launch, aiming to enhance your gameplay experience. Let's dive right in!

[b]Major Update: Adjusted and Optimized Task Tick Framework![/b]

other important Update(s) and fix(es):
[list]
[*] Update: Optimized the time required for level reset.
[*][b] Update: Added a language menu shortcut button.[/b]
[*] Update: Some UI icons.
[*] Fix: Corrected some issues with incorrect localized English text.
[*] Fix: An issue where certain prompts wouldn't appear when loading saves.
[*] Fix: An issue where the Task Tick information panel might display multiple identical entries.
[/list]

[h3]Added a language menu shortcut button：[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/243387a6a71d91a0c5963a43d79edd760c6bbde7.png[/img]

[h3]Updated some UI icons：[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/8857b64fb4879904b3242fd2adecc1f512d348f4.png[/img]

[h3]Regarding the details of the new task framework:[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/ccc74d9e67a070c63e08572738378a5d58eb23e9.png[/img]

The distinction between [b]Tick Version Task[/b] and [b]Set Version Task[/b] is [b][u]no longer present[/u][/b]; both categories have been integrated.
Each type of task now has a time division into [b]Deploy[/b] and [b]Check[/b].
During [b]Deploy[/b], specific objectives for the task will be displayed, and/or resources provided by the task system will be generated.
During [b]Check[/b], the system will reward players according to the task's requirements.
Moreover, now a task can offer multiple [i]Starcoins[/i] upon Task Check.

While there have been adjustments to the task-related rules and corresponding levels have been tweaked, rest assured, [u][b]that level progress remains unaffected after the update[/b][/u].

As for the Voucher missions, [u][b]those already completed will remain unaffected[/b][/u].
However, the highest score records for [b]incomplete [/b]Task Tick Voucher missions will be reset.

So, no need to worry at all – [u][b]this update doesn't require re-completion of any levels[/b][/u].
Still, we recommend players who have already completed previous task moment tutorials to give them a quick revisit and check the relevant info on the wiki page!

That's the scoop on this update! And guess what? There are even more exciting new levels and mechanics in the works that we can't wait to unveil.

Stay tuned and keep the excitement alive!

notes.title: Introduction to Key Mechanics: Units, Signals, Ticks, Shops
notes.notes:
As a puzzle game that brings pure gaming joy through its gameplay mechanics, "R.O.O.T." has several noteworthy features. Let me introduce these mechanics and their characteristics.

(P.S. The game will have a detailed in-game wiki encyclopedia. Here, I will focus on the interesting aspects of these mechanics without providing extensive explanations.)

[h3]Units:[/h3]
The most fundamental components in the game are units. The core unit acts as the power source, while the field units function as appliances and wires. Field units need to be connected to the core unit to receive signals and generate profits. Players need to use simple directional movements and rotations to connect these components and create more complex networks. Units can also have different levels, with higher-level components generating greater profits. Some units may have restrictions like limited lifespan or being locked in position, which tests the player's basic movement and arrangement skills.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/b3a784bef7df9083b53b81a533b2f70752454477.png[/img]

[h3]Signals:[/h3]
Different components generate different signals, and each signal has its own set of rules for calculating profits. Matrix signals are the simplest, requiring units to be directly or indirectly connected to the core unit to generate corresponding profits. Cluster signals require a more compact arrangement with a higher number of adjacent units. On the other hand, Thermo signals work in reverse, generating higher profits when there are fewer units adjacent in all eight directions. There are also more tricky Firewall signals, where profits are maximized when nearby units are exactly two in number.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/ef7f0325d15fa2344af0cfba1a67c2232e00eb38.png[/img]

[h3]Ticks:[/h3]
As the name suggests, "Ticks" are gameplay elements that test players' short-term strategies and adaptability. Similar to event cards in many board games, "Ticks" can be somewhat predictable to a certain extent, and players can actively trigger the progression of "Ticks". These may bring profits, special tasks, or even disasters.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/1110daf68698c3f039c4cc4d27f8860e5a885793.png[/img]

[h3]Shops:[/h3]
The "Shops" mechanism in the later stages is an interesting one. Unlike other mechanics that impose more restrictions, the shop gives players more choices. Players can purchase units of different types and levels, each with a different price. Moreover, players can place the purchased units in specific rows or columns or even at random positions, adding a touch of uncertainty to the situation.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43459195/d76fba0ce6030a0dc7d81d15f6e2592f2fa9761a.png[/img]

The game will be available tomorrow, and I look forward to meeting all of you. See you then!

notes.title: Countdown to the Early Access
notes.notes:
Hello, players!

Time flies by, and it feels like it was just a short while ago when we announced the release date. Now, we're less than 48 hours away from that moment.

After three years of hard work, we have finally transformed a simple entry into a game that is ready for launch on STEAM. It's truly an awe-inspiring journey.

The "Early Access" version will include around 90 levels, featuring various gameplay mechanics. You'll also get a glimpse of the unfolding world and the story of the first act through the narrative.

We will continue to update and improve the game until its official release. The complete version will have approximately 150 levels, and the story will have a satisfying conclusion. Moreover, there will be an abundance of new mechanics, signals, and types of challenges. We'll enhance the UI, music, sound effects, and gradually add more practical features.

We are eagerly looking forward to the game's launch in two days, and we hope you are too!

We would explain the updated "Adjacent Units" Concept here explictly.

Adjacent units were originally defined as: [i]eight-directional neighbouring activated same-signal field units[/i].
However, after our re-view of relevant rules. We came to the conclusion that this definition needs to be adjusted.
The concept of "Adjacent Unit" is now: "[b]eight-directional neighbouring unit[/b]".
In other words, the concept has transformed into physical adjacency only, no longer consider signal-realted properties of other units anymore.
